CHIEF COMPLAINT
Anxiety management follow-up and general preventive health maintenance.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 45-year-old woman presenting for follow-up. She reports that her anxiety has improved significantly since starting Buspar prescribed by Dr. Brown. She experienced severe anxiety in November and December that was debilitating, which prompted the medication initiation. She notes that her anxiety typically started during work hours and would spike randomly without apparent reason. She recalls that in November and December, her anxiety would worsen the week before her menstrual period, then progressed to random spikes. She was on progesterone during this time period for menstrual regulation. She attributes some of her anxiety to work stress, specifically related to leading the process of delivering COVID-19 results to patients and opening evaluation centers and COVID clinics at the beginning of the pandemic. She also felt guilty and stressed about not being on the front lines like physicians and nurses in the ICU. She notes that Dr. Ward prescribed Singulair and mentioned it could cause anxiety. Patient discontinued Camila birth control after noting significantly increased hunger and constant eating; since stopping, she feels better and has lost some weight over the past six months. She denies other current issues.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies weight loss currently, though reports weight loss over the past six months. Denies other acute symptoms. Reports breast tenderness in the left breast and states that breast lumps feel smaller but are still present. Reports continued itching/discomfort in pelvic area managed with topical cream used once weekly with good effect. Denies any other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Anxiety disorder (recently treated with Buspar)
Menstrual irregularity (treated with progesterone)
Breast lumps/cysts
Pelvic itching/discomfort
History of abnormal Pap smear in 2009 (required surveillance every six months at that time, subsequently normalized)

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (for anxiety)
Progesterone (for menstrual regulation)
Topical cream for pelvic itching/discomfort (used once weekly)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age approximately 45.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works in healthcare/laboratory setting involved with COVID-19 testing and patient result delivery. She underwent significant workplace stress related to pandemic response and process implementation. Husband and daughter have not received COVID-19 vaccine due to concerns about future health impacts. Patient and son have received COVID-19 vaccine (son has had first dose).

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Neck: Palpable small bumps noted; patient states they are smaller than previously.
Breast: Left breast feels slightly denser than right. Tenderness elicited on left breast examination where patient indicated. Patient notes lumps feel smaller than before but are still palpable. No acute changes noted.
Pelvic: Exam appears normal. Patient confirms continued use of topical cream with weekly application providing relief.

RESULTS
Pap smear last performed in 2019 with negative/negative results. Repeat Pap smear ordered today.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Well-controlled on Buspar. Continue current management.
2. Breast lumps/cysts: Stable, no change from previous examination. Patient counseled that benign breast findings (cysts, lumps, fibroadenomas) are common and do not indicate cancer; cancer would present with change. Continue surveillance. Referred to breast specialist for ongoing management and potential office-based ultrasound evaluation. Specialist will contact patient within couple of business days to schedule appointment.
3. Menstrual regulation: Continue progesterone.
4. Pelvic itching/discomfort: Continue topical cream. Prescription to be refilled.
5. Preventive health: Repeat Pap smear ordered given history of prior abnormality and to screen for potential increased risk related to immune stress and pandemic-related health impacts.
6. Patient counseled on surveillance approach and reassured regarding breast findings.
